description: Work recorded during a request and executed later by a worker, so the response does not wait for it.
Each worker runs at most N jobs at once. Slots protect databases and third-party rate limits.
Durable queues may run a job more than once (a worker crashed before acknowledging). Handlers must tolerate it.
Running it twice has the same effect as once: check stored state first and use idempotency keys with external APIs.
Where jobs go after their last failed attempt, to be inspected, fixed and replayed instead of retried forever.
Writing the job into a table in the same transaction as the data change, so the two cannot get out of sync.
